subject: DPA Q&A: temporal hold vs erase trigger + geo-fallback evidence and certification
messages:
From: Aurora Security <security@aurora-corp.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@aurora-corp.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA Qs: temporal hold vs erase trigger + geo fallback evidence

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. A couple of follow-ups from the security team as we prepare redlines for the DPA:

1) Temporal/legal hold: we need clarity on how a legal/preservation hold would pause your erase workflow. Specifically:
   - If a customer requests preservation, do backups/snapshots for that tenant get excluded from scheduled erasure?
   - Is there a documented process we can reference that shows hold request -> hold accepted -> hold cleared?

2) Geo-fallback / onshore access: in cases where EU residency is required but operational recovery requires onshore intervention, what controls/notifications exist? We need to confirm that no customer data is permanently moved out of EU except for transient administrative access and that such access is logged/limited.

3) Proof of erasure: what artifacts can Redwood provide as certified evidence when deletion is complete? Examples we expect: delete manifests, snapshot/tombstone records, audit log slices, and a short statement of scope (what was deleted, when, which replicas).

I've attached our questionnaire (aurora_security_questionnaire_v2.pdf) with the exact DPA clauses we are looking to close. Can you reply with a short operational summary and any evidence examples you can commit to?

Best,
Alina Costa
Head of Security, Aurora Corp
security@aurora-corp.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Aurora Security <security@aurora-corp.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, contracts@aurora-corp.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA Qs: temporal hold vs erase trigger + geo fallback evidence

Alina — thank you for the clear list. Quick operational summary and next steps below. Attaching our operational playbook (redwood_erase_playbook_v1.docx) for reference.

High level answers:
- Legal/temporal hold: we support an explicit hold flag at the tenant level. When a hold is active, scheduled erasure jobs will skip the tenant across all layers (primary, snapshots, backups) until the hold is cleared. Holds are surfaced to ops via the console and generate an audit entry.

- Geo-fallback / administrative access: we do not permanently relocate customer datasets. Transient access by onshore support is performed against a read-only recovery snapshot, and only after 2-step approval (CS+Security) that is logged. We can restrict this flow to EU-only engineers for customers that request it.

- Proof of erasure / artifacts we can provide:
   * Erasure manifest (tenant id, objects scanned, objects deleted, timestamp)
   * Snapshot tombstone record with hash and deletion timestamp
   * Audit log extract showing the erase job id and operator/system events
   * Optional signed statement of completion for the defined scope

What I need from you to firm this up for the DPA:
- Which of the artifacts above is minimally acceptable for Aurora as "certified erasure"?
- Any specific retention window you need for evidence (e.g., keep manifests for X months)?

Next steps: I've looped in Kimberly (legal ops) to confirm the DPA language implications and Irene (security ops) to confirm the exact log extracts we can produce. We can paste suggested DPA language back in one round.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
(attachment: redwood_erase_playbook_v1.docx)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com, security@aurora-corp.com, contracts@aurora-corp.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jul 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA Qs: temporal hold vs erase trigger + geo fallback evidence

Alina / team — quick legal/ops clarification from our side. High-level notes you can expect in a DPA clause and operational commitments: 

Operational guarantees we commit to (proposed DPA wording to follow):

- Hold handling: "Customer-initiated legal holds will suspend automated deletion processes for the scope identified in the hold request. Redwood will retain associated manifests and deletion records until the hold is released."

- Transient administrative access: "Administrative access for recovery shall be performed against time-limited recovery snapshots, require dual-approval by Redwood CS and Redwood Security, and be logged. No customer content will be made persistently available outside the EU region."

- Proof/evidence: Redwood can provide an evidence package consisting of: erasure manifest (CSV), tombstone log extract, and an audit log slice for the erase job. We can retain evidence packages for up to 12 months by default; longer retention negotiated (e.g., 24 months) is possible as an addendum.

Notes and open items:
- Backups & third-party copies: we will include language that backups subject to operational SLA are covered by the same hold. However, we need to confirm Aurora's expected maximum restore/retention windows and whether those should be called out explicitly.

- Certification language: Aurora asks for a "certified erasure" statement. We can provide a signed attestation of the evidence package scope; we prefer to avoid full-blown external certification (audit) as a standard deliverable. We can discuss this as a scope addon.

Irene: can you confirm the exact format of the audit slice (fields and sample) so we can attach a sample in the next mail?

Kimberly Park
Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DPA Qs: temporal hold vs erase trigger + geo fallback evidence

Kimberly / Mateo — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. A few items from the legal team after reviewing your commitments: 

1) We appreciate the hold suspension language. For the DPA redline, Aurora will propose a short clause that requires Redwood to maintain the evidence package for a minimum of 12 months after the hold is cleared, and to notify Aurora within 48 hours of hold clearance if any erasures were postponed during the hold.

2) On the certified statement: Aurora requests a signed attestation template be added as an Annex. We understand the difference between attestation and third-party certification; the attestation should enumerate the artifacts provided.

3) Geo-fallback: we will accept the dual-approval operational control, but require that Redwood document the list of roles permitted to request onshore recovery (and provide a log sample).

Attached is our suggested redline (aurora_dpa_redline_proposal.docx) with exact clause language for the above. Please confirm if Redwood can accept or propose edits by EOD Mon (2028-07-24).

Regards,
Marcus Lemaire
Senior Counsel, Aurora Corp
contracts@aurora-corp.com
